items.briefing:
A new phishing toolkit called "NovaCookies" is being sold online for as little as $320 a month, allowing criminals to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts even when two-factor authentication is enabled — a serious risk for any organisation using Microsoft 365, including RTOs. Separately, a recent case in the US serves as a reminder that foreign governments may use seemingly ordinary individuals to collect sensitive information, highlighting the importance of being mindful about what you share publicly or with strangers.

On a positive note, LevelBlue has opened a new security operations centre in Sydney, expanding local cybersecurity support for Australian organisations. **Practical tip:** If your organisation uses Microsoft 365, ask your IT team about enabling phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys or hardware security keys, for an extra layer of protection.

featured.title: LevelBlue opens Sydney security centre for Australia
featured.summary: Australian critical infrastructure operators gain local cyber response as tighter incident-reporting rules lift demand for onshore support.
